provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Out family batch. Aimed at design-and-install firms, not mowing crews; buyers decide on the design process, plants and how the garden survives year one. No nursery or plant-brand names. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Landscape design process and plan fee
pageStructurePlus.contains: The consult, site and soil walk, the planting plan and rendering, revision rounds, the design fee and how it credits toward the install
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers fear paying for a plan they can't afford to build. Showing the steps and the credit is what gets the paid consult booked.

pageStructurePlus.section: Plants by sun, soil and season
pageStructurePlus.contains: Full-sun and shade beds, wet and dry spots, deer-resistant choices, what blooms in which month, and evergreen structure for winter
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners decide on how the garden will look in their conditions. A plant page shows you design for their yard, not a catalogue.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Native plantings, pollinator beds, lawn reduction, drip irrigation, rain gardens for downspouts, and what upkeep a native garden really needs
pageStructurePlus.why: A growing share of buyers ask for native or low-water gardens. A page that explains them well wins that buyer outright.

pageStructurePlus.section: Planting day and the first year
pageStructurePlus.contains: Bed prep, soil amendment, planting, mulch, edging, the first-year watering schedule, the plant replacement warranty, and the follow-up visit
pageStructurePlus.why: New gardens die from watering mistakes in the first summer. Owners trust the installer who plans for that.

pageStructurePlus.section: Front-yard planting and curb appeal refresh
pageStructurePlus.contains: Foundation plantings, walkway borders, a new bed line, specimen trees, uplighting, and a smaller one-week install scope
pageStructurePlus.why: A front-yard refresh is the easiest first job to sell and often leads to the full backyard design.

designDirections.name: Fresh Beds
designDirections.bestFor: Smaller install crews selling front-yard refreshes and planting jobs on a fast estimate
designDirections.whyItFits: Olive and a bookish serif feel like a garden notebook, and the plain layout keeps the estimate button in reach.

designDirections.name: Season by Season
designDirections.bestFor: Design-install firms with finished gardens to show at planting and a season later
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's combo. Brick and linen let green planting carry the colour, and slab headings feel like a garden plan's title block.

designDirections.name: Estate Garden
designDirections.bestFor: Landscape design studios selling full-property master plans and phased installs
designDirections.headlineSample: Landscape design for {City} homes and estates
designDirections.whyItFits: Ivory and antique gold with an old-style serif read like a design studio, suited to buyers paying for the plan before the plants.

openers.line: Your Maps listing has no site, so anyone searching for landscape design in {City} sees your phone number but none of your gardens. A design client picks the firm whose planting they like.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a garden buyer would see behind that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your link goes to Facebook, where the best garden you planted this spring sits between weather posts and a truck for sale. A design client wants to see planting plans and finished beds side by side.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest garden they posted.
openers.linkLine: Your landscape design work on its own site: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Site reads like a mowing company
openers.line: Your site leads with mowing and cleanups, but your Instagram is full of designed gardens. People searching for landscape design scroll past a mowing page.
openers.hook: Compare the site's home page with their grid. If design work is only on social, use this.
openers.linkLine: A site that leads with your garden design work: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone your garden gallery is cropped so the planting beds are cut off at the edges. People browse landscape ideas on a phone more than anywhere else.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your gardens, shown properly on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to request a landscape design consult except calling. Buyers want to send the yard size, sun and shade, and what they hate about the current beds first.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for a consult form. If none, use this.
openers.linkLine: A design consult form that asks sun, soil and wish list: {demo-link}

openers.line: You post gardens on planting day and then again when they fill in a season later. Those pairs are the best proof a landscape designer can show, and they're scattered across your feed.
openers.hook: Find a garden they posted twice: at planting and later. Mention it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your gardens at planting and a season on: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention a garden that looks good in every season and a designer who listened. That reassurance stays on your listing where a new client may never see it.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about the design or plants. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the gardens they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring planting calendars fill from designs drawn in late winter. The landscape designers people find in February are the ones planting in April.
openers.hook: Use from January to early March, or late summer for autumn planting. Name the season.

openers.line: People decide to redo the front beds on a Saturday afternoon, staring at them from the driveway. A consult request that works then catches the landscaping buyer before Monday.
openers.hook: Call the listed number on a weekend. If it hits a full or generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A landscape consult request that works on a weekend: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a landscape crew lead. Good plantsmen look at a firm's finished gardens before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note role and date.
openers.linkLine: A landscape company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You design gardens across several towns around {City}, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you'll come there. 'Landscape design' plus the town is what they type.
openers.hook: Find towns in their captions or reviews; use the one furthest from their yard.
openers.linkLine: A landscape page for each town you design in: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you let clients phase a landscape install or pay over time, say so on the design page. A full backyard plan is often built in two or three seasons.
openers.hook: Only if they mention phasing or financing publicly. Otherwise skip.
openers.linkLine: Phased landscape installs explained up front: {demo-link}

openers.line: Landscape buyers worry about plants dying the first summer and about crews on their property. Your insurance and a clear plant warranty on one page settles both.
openers.hook: Look for any mention of a plant warranty or insurance. Note what exists; never invent terms.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and plant warranty, stated plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: A newly planted front garden gets neighbours stopping on their walk to ask who did it. They still look up the landscape firm before calling.
openers.hook: Look for comments or reviews mentioning a neighbour. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next garden referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted has beautiful layering, tall at the back and soft at the edge. That garden should open your portfolio.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished garden and name it: style, key plants, the town if tagged.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} is a lovely planting, really well layered.

I was looking for landscape designers in {City} and found {Business Name} on Instagram, but no site where someone can see your gardens and request a design consult. I mocked up a sample landscape site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would you like to see it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got lost. Here's the sample landscape design site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It shows gardens at planting and a season later, has a consult form that asks sun, soil and wish list, and a page on the first year after planting. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for landscape design firms in {City}. I sent you a message about a sample site. Did you see it?"

IF NO:
"No problem. It's a sample site for {Business Name} that leads with your designed gardens, with a design consult form and a plant warranty page, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, then ask how much of their work is design versus maintenance
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many garden and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For your firm I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is less than the plants in one front bed."
"Can we go through it for ten minutes this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before planting season."

objections.handler: "Referrals are the best clients. They still look your gardens up before the consult, and a site that shows plans and finished beds makes the design fee feel obvious."

objections.objection: We do a lot of maintenance; I don't want more mowing calls.
objections.handler: "Then the site leads with design and install and says plainly you don't take mowing-only work. The consult form filters the rest."
"Great. Happy to hand over the garden gallery layout and the consult form. If it hasn't happened by planting season, the offer stands."
"That's why the design process page explains your fee and how it credits toward the install. Buyers who read it arrive expecting to pay."
"Perfect timing. Gardens are designed in winter and planted in spring. The site is working by the time the planting calendar fills."
"{Build Range}. For you around {Build Price}: a garden portfolio, a consult form, a plants page and a few town pages. Less than one specimen tree, planted."

email.subject: Landscape design site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for landscape designers in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll email the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, the {Business Name} landscape demo is coming down Friday.

Would you like it kept up? One word is enough.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, garden design season is starting and the planting calendar fills fast after this. Thought of {Business Name}.

The sample site is still up and the price hasn't changed: {demo-link}

bullets: Price the portfolio by garden, not by page. Each finished landscape is its own story with planting-day and later views.
A design consult form that asks sun, soil, budget and wish list is the most valuable piece; price it on its own line.
Peg the build to the plant material in one front-yard refresh, never to hours.
Add a design process and fee page only for firms that charge for plans; skip it for install-only crews.
Plant pages are cheap to add one at a time and keep earning searches; sell them as a monthly add.
Leave maintenance-only services off the build so the site attracts design buyers.

lineItems.description: Max with planting-day and season-later pairs, a plant list and a short design write-up.

lineItems.item: Design consult form with sun, soil and wish list
lineItems.description: Max with picture upload, budget bands, style picks and routing to the designer.
Max with bloom calendar, sun and soil notes and a gallery of the plant in their gardens.
Max with a rain garden explainer, a drip irrigation section and a local native plant list.
Max when each town page gets local gardens and soil or deer notes.
Max when plans are paired with the finished garden from the same yard.

whatElseYouSell.name: Planting-day and season-later garden shoot
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Shoot a garden the day it's planted and again when it fills in. Those two visits give your landscape portfolio its strongest pairs."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2 for the first visit, then a return visit a season later.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts of finished gardens
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Each week a finished bed or garden goes on your Maps profile with the key plants and the town named."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks when the garden first blooms
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When the new planting has its first bloom, the client gets a note asking for a review while they're proudest of the garden."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, timed to bloom after each install.

whatElseYouSell.name: Late-winter landscape design campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A February push for spring garden designs fills your consult calendar before the nurseries open."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in December, run January through March.

whatElseYouSell.name: Yard signs at new gardens
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A small garden sign in a new front bed for a few weeks, with your name and the site, answers the 'who did your landscaping' question for you."

whatElseYouSell.name: Seasonal garden newsletter for past clients
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short seasonal note to past clients on pruning, bulbs and what's blooming brings back add-on beds and referrals."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once there's a client list.

whatElseYouSell.name: Garden tour open day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A past client opens their garden for an afternoon in bloom season, and prospects booked through the site see your landscaping in person."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 6, in peak bloom, with a willing client.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The nursery you buy shrubs from has customers asking who can plant it all. A site with a designer referral page helps both of you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Nurseries have budgets and walk-in traffic, and the landscape client is a steady wholesale buyer.

withoutAI.whoPays: The hardscaper, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Whoever builds the patios inside your garden designs needs a site too. One intro from you and both sites point to each other."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Design-install firms sub or partner on hardscape constantly; the referral is warm.

withoutAI.whoPays: The irrigation contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The irrigation tech who adds drip to your new beds needs a booking site. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Every new garden needs water. The irrigation contractor depends on the landscape firm's referrals.

withoutAI.route: Arborists who prune around your gardens
withoutAI.whoPays: The tree service, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The arborist who thins canopies so your shade beds get light is on the same jobs. Their site can send garden work your way."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Tree and garden work overlap on every mature property.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Agents call for a quick front-yard planting before the listing photos. A vendor page for their sellers puts your landscaping on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents refer vendors daily and pay for pages that make them look organised.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The local garden club runs tours and talks with a flyer and an email list. A simple events and membership site helps them, and you speak there."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small budgets but high trust, and every member is a landscape buyer.

withAI.route: Plant picker assistant for the nursery
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers describe their sun, soil and deer, and the assistant suggests plants the nursery actually stocks, with a 'have it planted' link."
withAI.whyItWorks: It sells more plants and sends planting work to the landscape client.

withAI.route: Drip zone planner for the irrigation contractor
withAI.pitchLine: "From the planting plan, the assistant drafts drip zones and emitter counts for the irrigation tech to check."
withAI.whyItWorks: It speeds the irrigation quote on every new garden the landscape firm installs.

withAI.pitchLine: "The agent uploads a tired front yard and gets a clearly labelled preview with new planting beds, to show the seller before calling the installer."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents like quick seller conversations; the preview ends with a landscape referral.

withAI.route: Event and membership assistant for the garden club
withAI.pitchLine: "Members ask about garden tour dates and dues by email. An assistant answers from the club's calendar and handles sign-ups."
withAI.whyItWorks: Volunteer-run clubs need help, and the designer gains goodwill with buyers.

withAI.pitchLine: "Resident landscaping requests get checked against the HOA's plant and front-yard rules before the committee sees them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Committees want fewer resubmissions; the manager pays for the time saved.

withAI.route: Pruning schedule assistant for the arborist
withAI.pitchLine: "Customers describe their trees and the assistant suggests when to prune and books the visit, flagging garden beds nearby."
withAI.whyItWorks: Arborists book better seasons, and garden beds get flagged for the landscape client.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for garden enquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Calls you miss while planting get a text asking whether it's a new garden design, a bed refresh or maintenance, so you call the design jobs back first."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and the wording approved.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for landscape jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review gets a reply drafted that mentions the garden and a plant or two by name, ready to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Landscape budget guide by scope
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Buyers choose front refresh, backyard beds or full design-install and a yard size, and see a realistic landscaping range before the consult."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price bands by scope and their minimum project.

softwareAI.name: Design fee and install deposit billing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Design fee at booking, install deposit on approval of the planting plan, balance at walkthrough, each invoiced automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their fee rules and payment account.

softwareAI.name: Plant list drafter from the consult notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From the consult form, sun and soil notes and the client's style picks, it drafts a starting garden plant list from your own palette for you to edit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their go-to plant palette by condition. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: First-year watering reminder texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New garden clients get watering reminders through the first summer, more in heat waves. Fewer dead plants, fewer warranty replacements."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their watering guidance and the install dates.

softwareAI.name: Project board from consult to walkthrough
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every landscape job from consult to plan approval, plant order, install and the follow-up visit on one board."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their stages and who designs versus installs.

softwareAI.name: After-hours garden consult booking line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers evening calls, asks about the yard and the style of garden they want, screens out mowing-only requests, and books the consult."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their calendar, consult fee and screening rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Plant order and nursery pickup sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The approved planting plan turns into an order sheet by nursery with sizes and counts, and a pickup checklist for the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their usual nurseries and plan format.

softwareAI.name: Garden chatbot on plants, deer and upkeep
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'what grows in my shady side yard' and 'will deer eat this' from your own plant notes, and books a consult for anything bigger."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their plant notes and current lead time. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Client portal with plan approval and plant warranty
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients approve the planting plan, see install dates, and file a plant warranty claim with a picture instead of calling."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the project board in place.

softwareAI.name: Garden concept preview from a yard picture
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The client uploads their bare front yard and sees a clearly labelled concept of new beds and planting to react to before the design consult."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a set of their finished gardens and their palette. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal enhancement offer sequence
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Past garden clients get a spring bed refresh and an autumn bulb offer at the right moment. That's add-on planting from people who already trust you."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the past client list and their seasonal offers.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to planting plan scope
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the property, talk through beds, edging and trees, and it drafts the landscape scope and estimate for you to finish."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their estimate template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Garden story writer for portfolio pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "From your notes and plant list it drafts the story for each finished garden page, which you approve before it publishes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their notes and sign-off. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Plant warranty tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Tracks every planted shrub and tree by job and date, so warranty replacements are checked against the terms and the watering log."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their warranty terms and plant lists by job.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by garden scope
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See whether front refreshes, backyard beds or full design-installs actually pay best once plants, soil, mulch and crew days are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs a season of nursery invoices and crew days.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with planting checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew checks off bed prep, planting depth, mulch and edging with a picture per bed, so the designer sees each garden without driving out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, with two crews. Needs their install checklist and a lead to pilot.

softwareAI.name: Commercial landscape bid sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Bids for HOA entrances and office plantings come together on one sheet with plant counts, insurance and references."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, for firms chasing commercial installs. Needs two past bids.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for landscape crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Landscape applicants say whether they know plants, can run a skid steer and have a licence, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they hire. Needs must-haves and pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Landscape budget guide sold to design-install firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "The landscaping budget guide that stopped one firm's free-design requests works for every designer whose consults stall at the first number."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the logic; others load their own price bands.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Designer referral network for a wholesale nursery
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Homeowners who visit your retail yard ask who can design their garden. A directory of trade landscape designers who buy from you answers that."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Growers want loyal trade buyers and lack a homeowner channel.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members get a garden portfolio, design consult form and plant warranty page, ready to switch on."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One deal reaches dozens of landscape firms who trust the association.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies with landscaping clients rebuild the same portfolio and consult form each time. License the finished garden template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the client; you supply the trade-specific part.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The native plant society or conservation group
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members want native gardens installed and don't know who does it well. A directory of vetted native-garden installers serves the mission."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Conservation groups have grant money for outreach, and the landscape client is the first listing.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The water utility or stormwater district
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents apply for the rain garden rebate, upload the site and get matched with approved garden installers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Utilities fund these programs and need completed applications. The designer knows the install side.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Buyers want more than the builder-grade shrubs. A landscape upgrade options page sells planting packages before closing."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders like option revenue and organised partners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each managed community gets one page for planting requests, dead shrub reports and seasonal colour approvals."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Managers juggle grounds requests by email; one portal covers every property.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your franchisees all plant different gardens but send buyers to one corporate page. Give each owner a local portfolio and consult flow that feeds their own calendar."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Seasonal plant availability note for designers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly note on which shrubs and perennials are scarce or plentiful, built from availability lists designers share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Designers plan around shortages; contributed data keeps it honest.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The landscape design slot in each metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A landscape firm in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I take one garden design firm per metro, so the portfolio and consult flow stay unique. In your metro that slot is still open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusive territory lets you reuse the template and pitch.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rebuild landscape sites stuck on mowing templates
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The design firm with the wrong site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "If your site was built for a mowing company and buries your gardens, I can move you onto a design-first landscape template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These owners already know their site is wrong; they need someone who gets design buyers.

upsellLadder.offer: Landscape site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The landscape site and the care plan go on one contract, so adding a finished garden is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks at first bloom and Google profile posts
upsellLadder.trigger: The first garden installed since launch has its first bloom.
upsellLadder.line: "That garden just bloomed. Let's ask for the review and post it while it looks its best."

upsellLadder.trigger: A full install is scheduled, or the portfolio still has only a few gardens.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot your next garden on planting day and come back when it fills in. Those pairs sell design."

upsellLadder.trigger: Consult requests show buyers with no budget in mind, or consults that end at the design fee.
upsellLadder.line: "Those consults that stalled at the number are what this fixes. Buyers see the landscaping range first."

upsellLadder.trigger: A warranty replacement caused by underwatering, or a heat wave forecast.
upsellLadder.line: "That dead hydrangea was a watering problem. Reminders through the first summer save the next garden."

upsellLadder.offer: Project board from consult to walkthrough
upsellLadder.trigger: A plant order goes missing or they add a second install crew.
upsellLadder.line: "Two crews and a stack of planting plans need one board. Let's put every garden on it."

upsellLadder.trigger: Autumn arrives with a season of past garden clients on file.
upsellLadder.line: "Every garden you planted this year is ready for bulbs. One offer to past clients fills your autumn."
